source_user: Advanced cluster case RDMA-70: Explain how RDMA changes the data path for multi-node GPU training or inference. Variant 70 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate verbs, queues, memory registration, transport selection, bandwidth, latency, and fallback behavior; compare measured device counters with application-level communication time. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: For Variant 70, begin with a read-only, timestamped comparison and state hardware, topology, MTU, versions, transport, GPU-direct eligibility, registration permissions, message-size distributions, and unknowns. Trace the application operation through the communication library, verbs, work requests/completions, registered memory, queue pairs, NIC/link, and remote host/GPU. Explain that RDMA can reduce CPU copies but does not guarantee end-to-end benefit; distinguish GPU-direct from host staging and state fallback triggers. Define a falsifiable hypothesis for a pre-registered workload and threshold. Compare a matched non-RDMA baseline with warm-up exclusion, repetitions, and a fixed clock. Measure end-to-end latency, communication/overlap time, throughput, CPU use, bandwidth, p50/p95/p99, retries, timeouts, and relevant counters in compatible units; report uncertainty and control topology, clocks, batching, and concurrent load. Diagnose registration, completion, congestion, link loss, and fallback in order. Correlate counters with application traces. Test link failure only in an isolated environment, requiring error propagation, bounded retries, integrity checks, and a documented stop/restore threshold; redact sensitive telemetry and never change production without approval.
